category.wavefront.own_voice.description: The volume of your own voice

general.group.permeation: Classic Mode (only used when Sound Physics is off)

wavefront:config.raysCast.description:
How many invisible rays are fired from you to measure the space around you. They work out how big and echoey the place is.

Example: more rays give steadier reverb in caves.

Recommended: 200. Try 100 on a slow computer.

Performance cost: HIGH.
wavefront:config.raysBounced.description:
How many times each ray bounces off walls before it stops. More bounces = more reverb and a better sense of large spaces.

Recommended: 3.

Performance cost: HIGH.
wavefront:config.maxRayLength.description:
How far each ray travels, in chunks (16 blocks each).

Recommended: 4 chunks.

Performance cost: medium.
wavefront:config.procRange.description: Sounds further away than this are left exactly as vanilla Minecraft plays them. -1 means no limit.\n\nRecommended: 200 blocks.
wavefront:config.tickRate.description:
How often a sound that is still playing gets re-checked, in game ticks (20 ticks = 1 second). Lower = follows you more quickly as you move. 0 = never re-check.

Example: at 10, a jukebox adjusts twice a second as you walk round a building.

Recommended: 10. Try 5 for snappier response on a fast computer.

Performance cost: medium.
wavefront:config.soundMult.description: 1 is just default Minecraft sound dist\nPERFORMANCE IMPACT: HIGH
wavefront:config.volumeMultiplier.description: Makes every processed sound louder or quieter.\n\nRecommended: 1x.
wavefront:config.reverb.description:
Adds echo that matches the space you are in: none in an open field, a long tail in a big cave.

Recommended: ON.

Performance cost: medium.
wavefront:config.permeation.description: Classic mode only. The original method of muffling sound through walls. Sound Physics replaces it when that is ON.\n\nRecommended: ON.
wavefront:config.permeationStepSize.description: Classic mode only. How finely the original method measures the wall thickness. Smaller = more accurate and slower.\n\nRecommended: 0.0625 blocks.
wavefront:config.permeatedTickRate.description:
How often permeated sounds' positions should be updated
(0 is off)
(1 = every tick -> 20 = every second)
PERFORMANCE IMPACT: MEDIUM (higher than normal tickrate)
wavefront:config.attenuationType.description: Classic mode only. How sound fades with distance in the original Sound Physics Perfected method.\n\nRecommended: Vercidium Linear.
wavefront:config.rayBounce.description: Larger = less heavily the sound will be coming from walls (will make likely make sounds quieter)\nPERFORMANCE IMPACT: NONE
wavefront:config.debug.description:
Shows each processed sound's name on screen. With Sound Physics ON it also shows its volume factor, treble factor and path length.

Recommended: OFF. Useful for checking why something sounds the way it does.

Known issue from the original mod: Chat mode can crash with Sodium.
wavefront:config.maxBlocksPermeated.description: Classic mode only. Sound stops completely after passing through this many blocks.\n\nRecommended: 3 blocks.
wavefront:config.permeationAbsorption.description: Classic mode only. Volume is multiplied by this for every block of wall. Lower = walls block more.\n\nRecommended: 0.4.
wavefront:config.barrierAsAir.description: Classic mode only. Invisible barrier blocks do not muffle sound. Sound Physics always ignores barriers.\n\nRecommended: ON.
wavefront:config.shortcutDirectionality.description: Classic mode only. If nothing is between you and a sound, use its true direction instead of the ray-traced one.\n\nRecommended: ON.
wavefront:config.maxSounds.description: The most sounds the mod will work on at once. Sounds beyond this play as vanilla.\n\nRecommended: 100.
wavefront:config.bounceAbsorptionMultiplier.description: How much sound survives each bounce off a wall. 1.0 = nothing lost, 0.5 = half lost per bounce. Affects reverb.\n\nRecommended: 0.9.
wavefront:config.disableFXOnUI.description: Leaves button clicks and other menu sounds untouched. Some mods play world sounds in the same group, and those would be skipped too.\n\nRecommended: OFF.
wavefront:config.reverbTuning.description: Debug for finding what values are coming out of Blue ray casting.
wavefront:config.useExplosionResistance.description: Classic mode only. Guesses how much a block muffles sound from how blast-proof it is. Sound Physics uses a researched table per block instead.\n\nRecommended: ON.
wavefront:config.legacyReverb.description: Switches reverb mode to different versions TUNING IS NOT ALWAYS AVAILABLE
wavefront:config.experimentalReverb.description: Enables an experimental reverb which allows reverb to be louder than
wavefront:config.globalReverbIntensity.description: Overall reverb intensity multiplier\nHigher = more intense reverb
wavefront:config.indoorBias.description: Emphasis for indoor reverb characteristics\nHigher = more pronounced indoor reverb
wavefront:config.outdoorBias.description: Emphasis for outdoor reverb characteristics\nHigher = more pronounced outdoor reverb
wavefront:config.smallRoomEmphasis.description: Emphasis for small room characteristics\nHigher = more intimate small room feel
wavefront:config.largeRoomEmphasis.description: Emphasis for large room characteristics\nHigher = more spacious large room feel
wavefront:config.distanceAttenuationLinear.description: Linear distance attenuation factor\nHigher = sound drops off faster with distance
wavefront:config.distanceAttenuationQuadratic.description: Quadratic distance attenuation factor\nHigher = more realistic distance falloff
wavefront:config.airAbsorptionRate.description: How quickly air absorbs sound\nHigher = more muffled distant sounds
wavefront:config.roomVolumeMultiplier.description: Room volume estimation factor\nHigher = treats rooms as larger
wavefront:config.roomComplexityDivisor.description: Surface/volume complexity factor\nLower = treats rooms as more complex
wavefront:config.lateReverbDelayMultiplier.description: Late reverb delay vs early reflections\nHigher = later late reverb
wavefront:config.baseReverbGain.description: Minimum reverb gain\nHigher = always some reverb present
wavefront:config.reverbGainMultiplier.description: How much reverb strength affects final gain\nHigher = more responsive to reverb conditions
wavefront:config.maxOverallGain.description: Maximum overall reverb gain\nPrevents reverb from being too loud
wavefront:config.sendFilterHfReduction.description: High frequency reduction for send filter\nLower = more muffled reverb
wavefront:config.minDiffusion.description: Minimum reverb diffusion\nLower = more directional reflections
wavefront:config.maxDiffusion.description: Maximum reverb diffusion\nHigher = more scattered reflections
wavefront:config.minDensity.description: Minimum reverb density\nLower = more sparse reflections
wavefront:config.decayLfMultiplier.description: Low frequency decay ratio multiplier\nHigher = longer low frequency decay
wavefront:config.outdoorHfLeak.description: High frequency leak for outdoor spaces\nHigher = less muffled outdoor sound
wavefront:config.echoTimeMultiplier.description: Echo time based on room size\nHigher = longer echo times
wavefront:config.echoDepthMultiplier.description: Echo depth based on density\nHigher = more pronounced echoes
wavefront:config.modulationTimeMultiplier.description: Modulation time based on room size\nHigher = slower modulation
wavefront:config.modulationDepthMultiplier.description: Modulation depth based on enclosure\nHigher = more modulation
wavefront:config.baseHfReference.description: Base high frequency reference (Hz)\nHigher = affects higher frequencies
wavefront:config.hfRoomSizeFactor.description: How room size affects HF reference\nHigher = more room size influence
wavefront:config.baseLfReference.description: Base low frequency reference (Hz)\nHigher = affects higher low frequencies
wavefront:config.lfRoomSizeFactor.description: How room size affects LF reference\nHigher = more room size influence
wavefront:config.roomRolloffSizeFactor.description: How room size affects rolloff\nHigher = less room size influence on rolloff
wavefront:config.rt60SabineConstant.description: Sabine's RT60 formula constant\nPhysics constant - usually don't change
wavefront:config.minTotalAbsorption.description: Minimum absorption to prevent division by zero
wavefront:config.diffusionComplexityWeight.description: Weight of room complexity in diffusion calculation\nHigher = complexity affects diffusion more
wavefront:config.diffusionEnclosureWeight.description: Weight of enclosure in diffusion calculation\nHigher = enclosure affects diffusion more
wavefront:config.diffusionReverbWeight.description: Weight of reverb strength in diffusion calculation\nHigher = reverb strength affects diffusion more
wavefront:config.soundBlacklist.description: Sounds whose name contains any of these words are played exactly as vanilla. Part of a name is enough.\n\nExample: add 'rain' to leave rain sounds untouched.
wavefront:config.soundTickBlacklist.description: Sounds whose name contains any of these words are processed once when they start and never updated afterwards.
wavefront:config.voicechatReverb.description: Other players' voices echo to match the space, like game sounds do. Needs Simple Voice Chat.\n\nRecommended: ON.
wavefront:config.voicechatReverbSelf.description: Plays your own voice back to you with the room's echo.\n\nRecommended: OFF.
wavefront:config.voicechatMuffle.description:
Walls dull other players' voices. With Sound Physics ON, voices also bend round corners and through doorways.

Example: a friend behind a wall with an open doorway is quieter and duller, but understandable.

Recommended: ON.
wavefront:config.voicechatMuffleVolume.description: Walls make voices quieter as well as duller.\n\nRecommended: ON.
wavefront:config.wavePhysics.description:
The main switch. When ON, walls muffle sound according to what they are made of, and sound bends round corners and through doorways.

Example: a zombie behind a stone wall is faint and dull; step to where there is a gap and you hear it clearly, coming from the gap.

Recommended: ON. Turn OFF to go back to the classic Sound Physics Perfected behaviour.
wavefront:config.wallStrength.description:
How much walls block sound. Higher = walls block more. 0 = walls block nothing.

Example: at 1.0 a single stone block makes a sound about as quiet as it would really be through a metre of rock (very quiet). At 0.5 the same block takes off half as many decibels.

Recommended: 0.6. Raise it for realism, lower it if you rely on hearing mobs through cave walls.
wavefront:config.diffraction.description:
Lets sound travel round edges and through openings instead of only straight through walls. Low notes bend easily, high notes less, so sound round a corner is quieter and duller.

Example: a piston behind a free-standing wall is heard coming over the top of the wall, not muted by it.

Recommended: ON.

Performance cost: small to medium, only for sounds that are blocked.
wavefront:config.diffractionStrength.description:
How much quieter sound gets when it has to bend. Higher = corners cut more sound. 0 = bending costs nothing.

Example: at 1.0 the loss follows the real-world barrier formula.

Recommended: 1.0.
wavefront:config.diffractionRoutes.description:
How many different ways round an obstacle are added together for each sound.

Example: for a sound behind a wall, 3 lets it arrive over the top and round both ends.

Recommended: 3. Use 1 on a slow computer.

Performance cost: grows with this number.
wavefront:config.diffractionRange.description:
Sounds further away than this are not checked for ways round obstacles; they only get the through-the-wall sound.

Recommended: 32 blocks.

Performance cost: higher values mean more searching.
wavefront:config.diffractionSearchBudget.description:
How hard the mod looks for a way round before giving up. Higher finds routes through longer, twistier tunnels.

Recommended: 6000. Lower it if sealed rooms cause stutter.

Performance cost: medium when a sound is fully sealed in.
